reply:
I ported the program to Go, and `node check.mjs` passes all 6 example cases. `go vet` and the unit tests (which also cover words split across read boundaries) pass too.

I also checked it against the Python original. On a generated 50 MB input the output was byte-for-byte identical, and Go took 0.15s against Python's 0.55s. On 3 MB of random bytes the outputs were identical as well.

- **`main.go`**: the entry point. It exits with status 0 normally and status 1 only if reading or writing fails.
